alignments.note: One English negative word carries both the universal quantifier `כֹּל` and the negative `לֹא`, so the two share one discontinuous unit headed on the negative, which is what distinguishes *None* from *all* (rule 35).

Substantival participle with the supplied relative (rule 46); its bare object suffix is reached through the supplied *unto*, which belongs to the participle's unit (rule 44). Headed on the word carrying the lexeme.
Object suffix rendered by the object pronoun (rule 18).
`שׁוּב` rendered by the phrasal *return again*; the particle restates the returning the Hebrew verb itself writes, so it stays with the verb rather than being marked `added` (rule 44).
Paragogic nun has no English realization (rule 32).
Waw plus negative fused into one English word carrying both the coordination and the negation, headed on the negative (rule 35).
Finite verb with its fronted auxiliary and subject pronoun (rule 17); the bare direct object `אָרְחוֹת` is reached through the supplied *unto*, which belongs to the verb's unit (rule 44).

review_notes: *None* is read as rule 35's fusion of `כֹּל` with `לֹא`; the competing reading gives *None* to the negative alone and marks `כֹּל` `unrepresented`, but one English word here answers to both morphemes.
*again* is kept with `שׁוּב` because the return is what that verb writes; the competing reading marks it `added` under rule 44's surplus-particle sentence.
